source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which CAD risk factor is non-modifiable?
questions.rationale: Non-modifiable: family history, age, gender; others are modifiable.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CAD Risk Factors (PDF p. 306)
questions.quote: NON-MODIFIABLE RISK FACTORS

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which procedure places a device to keep a coronary artery open and prevent restenosis?
questions.rationale: Stents prevent closure and restenosis; atherectomy removes plaque; laser vaporizes plaque.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CAD Procedures (PDF p. 306)
questions.quote: Vascular stent to prevent the artery from closing and to prevent restenosis

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is a high HDL level protective against heart disease?
options: It carries lipids to the liver
questions.rationale: HDL transports lipoproteins to the liver for degradation and excretion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CAD (PDF p. 306)
questions.quote: a high HDL level is a strong protective factor

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which diet is recommended for a client with CAD?
questions.rationale: Low-calorie, low-sodium, low-cholesterol, low-fat diet with increased fiber.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, CAD Diet (PDF p. 306)
questions.quote: Increase in dietary fiber

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with heart failure has crackles, orthopnea, and pink frothy sputum. Which side is failing?
questions.rationale: Left-sided HF causes pulmonary congestion: dyspnea, crackles, orthopnea, pink frothy sputum.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Left-Sided HF (PDF p. 307)
questions.quote: Frothy, pink (blood-tinged) sputum

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Jugular vein distention, ascites, hepatomegaly, and leg edema indicate:
questions.rationale: Right-sided HF backs blood into systemic veins, causing JVD, edema, hepatomegaly, ascites.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Right-Sided HF (PDF p. 308)
questions.quote: Hepatomegaly (enlargement of the liver)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The most common cause of right ventricular failure is:
questions.rationale: Left-sided failure backs up into the lungs and then the right heart.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Right-Sided HF (PDF p. 308)
questions.quote: is the most common cause of right ventricular (RV) failure

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which assessment best evaluates fluid status in heart failure?
questions.rationale: Daily weight and I&O assess fluid overload and treatment response.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, HF Management (PDF p. 308)
questions.quote: weigh daily to assess for fluid overload

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In heart failure, angiotensin II worsens fluid overload by stimulating release of:
questions.rationale: Angiotensin II causes vasoconstriction and aldosterone release, retaining sodium and water.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Renin-Angiotensin System (PDF p. 308)
questions.quote: Angiotensin II also stimulates the release of aldosterone

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which ACC/AHA stage describes refractory end-stage heart failure?
questions.rationale: A: at risk; B: structural disease, no symptoms; C: symptoms; D: refractory end-stage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, HF Classification (PDF p. 307)
questions.quote: Patients with refractory end-stage heart failure requiring specialized interventions

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with heart failure on furosemide should be monitored for:
questions.rationale: Loop diuretics alter potassium; monitor K+ especially with digoxin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, HF Pharmacology (PDF p. 309)
questions.quote: these medications may alter the K+ level

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug class reduces afterload in heart failure?
questions.rationale: ACE inhibitors (captopril, enalapril) decrease afterload.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, HF Pharmacology (PDF p. 309)
questions.quote: Administer ACE inhibitors to decrease afterload

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug strengthens myocardial contractility in heart failure?
questions.rationale: Digoxin is a positive inotrope.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, HF Pharmacology (PDF p. 309)
questions.quote: Administer inotrope to strengthen myocardial contractility

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the usual cause of mitral stenosis?
questions.rationale: Mitral stenosis is usually from rheumatic heart disease causing fibrosis and calcification.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mitral Stenosis (PDF p. 309)
questions.quote: Usually due to rheumatic endocarditis

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A low-pitched rumbling diastolic murmur at the apex suggests:
questions.rationale: Mitral stenosis has a low-pitched rumbling diastolic murmur at the apex.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mitral Stenosis (PDF p. 309)
questions.quote: A Iow-pitched, rumbling, diastolic murmur is heard at the apex

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why may anticoagulants be prescribed for mitral stenosis?
questions.rationale: A dilated left atrium and atrial dysrhythmias raise thrombus risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mitral Stenosis Management (PDF p. 310)
questions.quote: may benefit from anticoagulants

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A high-pitched blowing systolic murmur at the apex indicates:
questions.rationale: Mitral regurgitation: high-pitched blowing systolic murmur at the apex.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mitral Regurgitation (PDF p. 310)
questions.quote: Systolic murmur is heard as a high- pitched, blowing sound at the apex

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A water-hammer (Corrigan's) pulse with widened pulse pressure is characteristic of:
questions.rationale: Aortic regurgitation causes bounding pulses and widened pulse pressure.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Aortic Regurgitation (PDF p. 311)
questions.quote: One characteristic sign of the disease is the water-hammer (Corrigan's) pulse

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with aortic stenosis faints during exertion. This is due to:
questions.rationale: Aortic stenosis causes syncope, angina, and exertional dyspnea from limited output.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Aortic Stenosis (PDF p. 311)
questions.quote: Syncope and dizziness because decreased circulation to the brain

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Small painful nodules on the finger pads of a client with endocarditis are:
questions.rationale: Osler's nodes are painful; Janeway lesions are painless macules on palms and soles.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Infective Endocarditis (PDF p. 311)
questions.quote: Small painful nodules (Osiers nodes) may be present in pads of fingers or toes

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Retinal hemorrhages with pale centers in infective endocarditis are called:
questions.rationale: Roth spots are emboli-related retinal hemorrhages.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Infective Endocarditis (PDF p. 311)
questions.quote: Hemorrhages with pale centers in the eyes caused by emboli (Roth spots)
